question.text: How many views will the top Netflix release receive in 2026 Christmas week?
question.resolution_criteria:
This question will resolve as the highest number of global views received by a Netflix English or non-English show or movie during the reporting week encompassing Christmas (December 25) 2026.

The source for this question will be the [Netflix Top 10](https://www.netflix.com/tudum/top10).
question.fine_print: This question refers to any show or movie available on Netflix, not just those produced by Netflix.

research:
I can't settle this yet. The Christmas week chart covers Mon Dec 21 to Sun Dec 27, 2026 and should come out around Dec 29. The front-runner looks like David Fincher's *The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth*, which starts streaming Wed Dec 23 and gets 5 days in that week. *Emily in Paris* S6 (Dec 24) and *Ray Gunn* (Dec 18) are the main rivals. Over the last three Christmas weeks the top title got 34.0M, 68.0M and 34.5M views.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-15: The Netflix Top 10 page shows the week of Nov 2-8, 2026. The top movie was *A Dog's Perfect Christmas* with 8.6M views. The data file behind the page shows the top show was *Taken: Natalee Holloway* S1 with 12.9M, and the top non-English title was *Collision Course* with 17.2M. [Tudum](https://www.netflix.com/tudum/top10), [TSV](https://www.netflix.com/tudum/top10/data/all-weeks-global.tsv)
- Weeks run Monday to Sunday. Dec 25, 2026 is a Friday, so the deciding week is Dec 21-27 (labelled "2026-12-27" in the file).

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has happened yet that settles this. Two weekly charts (Nov 9-15 and Nov 16-22) are still to come before even the December releases.

## 3. Recent news
- 2026-11-13: Season 2 of *Black Doves* became the No. 1 show globally on FlixPatrol. [Men's Journal](https://www.mensjournal.com/news/netflix-thriller-series-is-officially-the-no-1-show-in-the-world-one-week-after-new-season-drops)
- 2026-10: Regal and Cinemark won't show *Cliff Booth* in IMAX. Its exclusive IMAX run starts Nov 25 on more than 500 screens worldwide, then it reaches Netflix on Dec 23. I found no reviews yet. [Deadline](https://deadline.com/2026/10/further-mis-adventures-of-cliff-booth-regal-cinemark-1237209962/), [Collider](https://collider.com/further-mis-adventures-cliff-booth-imax-tickets-brad-pitt/)
- The December slate, per What's on Netflix:
  - *Ray Gunn* (Brad Bird, animated): Dec 18
  - *Cliff Booth*: Dec 23
  - *Emily in Paris* S6: Dec 24
  - Live NFL Christmas doubleheader: Dec 25 (Bills-Broncos and Packers-Bears)
  - Earlier in the month: *Bad Day* and Tyson Fury vs. Anthony Joshua on Dec 11
  - [WoN](https://www.whats-on-netflix.com/coming-soon/first-look-at-whats-coming-to-netflix-in-december-2026/)
- 2026: Gerwig's *Narnia* was first planned to start streaming Dec 25, 2026. It now opens in theaters Feb 12, 2027 and on Netflix Apr 2, 2027. [WoN](https://www.whats-on-netflix.com/news/netflixs-narnia-the-magicians-nephew-delayed-to-2027/)

## 4. Base rates (all from the Netflix data file)
**Top title in each Christmas week:**
- Week of Dec 25-31, 2023: *Rebel Moon Pt 1*, 34.0M, in its 2nd week. The week before it had 23.9M.
- Week of Dec 23-29, 2024: *Squid Game* S2, 68.0M in 4 days. The two Christmas NFL games had 14.4M and 14.3M.
- Week of Dec 22-28, 2025: *Stranger Things 5*, 34.5M, helped by Vol. 2 coming out Dec 25. Next: *The Great Flood* 33.1M, *The Grinch* 16.5M, *Emily in Paris* S5 13.3M. The 2025 NFL Christmas games are not on that week's chart, even though they reached about 30.5M (Lions-Vikings) and 22.4M (Cowboys-Commanders) global average viewers. That figure is not Netflix's "views" measure.

**Seasonal pattern:** mid-November tops were well below Christmas week each year.
- Nov 2025 tops around 29-34M (*Frankenstein*), then 34.5M at Christmas.
- 2024 rose sharply to 68M at Christmas.
- 2026 is running lower: the latest week's top is 17.2M, and the top was below 21.2M in each of the last four weeks.

**2026 peaks so far:** the highest weeks I saw were 34.1M (*I Will Find You*, Jun 28), 33.5M (*The Last House*), 33.4M (*The Whisper Man*), 31.1M and 30.8M (*Animals*).

**Comparable launches:**
- Movies after a theatrical run:
  - *Wake Up Dead Man* got 20.2M in its first 3 days (Fri release, Dec 2025) and 20.9M in week 2.
  - *Frankenstein* got 29.1M in its first week, then 33.8M.
  - *Glass Onion* released Dec 23, 2022 and logged 82.1M hours in its first 3 days. That was before Netflix reported views; roughly 35M views by my own conversion.
- *Emily in Paris* first weeks:
  - S4 Part 1 (2024): 19.9M
  - S5 (Dec 18, 2025, 4 days): 13.5M

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Kalshi, Polymarket or Manifold market for the Christmas week chart. The current markets cover only the Nov 17 chart. Kalshi prices the top show at about 9% for at least 9M views and 1% for at least 12M. *A Dog's Perfect Christmas* is about 96% to be top global movie.
- I found no expert forecasts.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Nov 25 onward: *Cliff Booth* IMAX run, with box office and reviews as a signal of demand.
- Dec 11: Fury vs. Joshua. For scale, Jake Paul vs. Joshua got 10.9M views in Dec 2025. It falls in an earlier week.
- Dec 18: *Ray Gunn* would be in its second week, which often beats the first.
- Dec 23: *Cliff Booth* (5 days in the week). Dec 24: *Emily in Paris* S6 (4 days).
- Dec 25: NFL doubleheader. It's unclear whether these games will be charted: 2024 counted them, 2025 did not.
- Dates may shift: the What's on Netflix schedule is an early look.
- Around Dec 29: the Christmas week chart is published.

- Dec 25: NFL games. They counted in the 2024 Top 10 but were absent in 2025, so whether they count again is unclear.
- Release dates could still slip, and the December schedule is described as provisional.

forecasts.reasoning:
**(a) Time left:** About 6 weeks. The Christmas week chart covers Mon Dec 21 to Sun Dec 27, 2026, and should be published around Dec 29.

**(b) Latest known value:** For the week of Nov 2-8, 2026, the top title was *Collision Course* with 17.2M views. The top show had 12.9M and the top English movie had 8.6M.

**(c) If nothing changed:** About 17M views. This is unrealistic, because the December releases are much stronger than the current mid-November titles.

**(d) If the trend continued:** Each year the top title rises from mid-November to Christmas, sometimes sharply. Recent Christmas week tops were 34.0M (2023), 68.0M (2024) and 34.5M (2025). The 2026 slate has three likely contenders:
- *Cliff Booth* gets 5 days in the week, plus Christmas viewing and a Brad Pitt / Fincher / Tarantino pedigree. I estimate roughly 25-45M.
- *Ray Gunn* is a Brad Bird animated family film in its second week, during school holidays. I estimate roughly 18-38M.
- *Emily in Paris* S6 gets 4 days. I estimate roughly 12-20M.
- The NFL games, if charted, would be about 14M.

The top is the maximum of these, so I put the median around 34M.

**(e) Historical variation:** Christmas week tops ranged from 34M to 68M over the last three years. Single releases can swing by a factor of 2 depending on reception, so uncertainty is wide.

**(f) Experts and markets:** There are no markets or expert forecasts for this week. The question creator's range of 15M-70M is consistent with the history above.

**(g) Unexpected scenarios:**
- Low: *Cliff Booth* gets mediocre reviews, its long runtime holds down the views count, and *Ray Gunn* underperforms. The top could then land around 18-22M, with *Emily* or *Ray Gunn* on top.
- High: *Cliff Booth* becomes a cultural event, like *Glass Onion* or *Happy Gilmore 2* scaled up to 5 holiday days, and reaches 50-65M. Alternatively, *Ray Gunn* takes off like *KPop Demon Hunters*.

**Tails:**
- 1st percentile: a release delay plus weak titles leaves a top near 15M.
- 99th percentile: a *Squid Game*-scale phenomenon near 75M.

(a) About 6 weeks remain. The Christmas week chart (Dec 21-27, 2026) should be published around Dec 29, and the question resolves around Dec 30.

(b) The latest known value is for the week of Nov 2-8, 2026: the top title was *Collision Course* with 17.2M views. The weekly top in 2026 has been under 21.2M for four straight weeks, and the 2026 peak so far is 34.1M.

(c) If nothing changed, the result would be about 17M. That is unrealistic, because the December slate is much stronger than current releases.

(d) If the seasonal trend continued, the result would be roughly 30-40M. Christmas week tops have been 34.0M, 68.0M and 34.5M, and that week always lifts above November levels. This year's main driver is *Cliff Booth*: a Fincher film starring Brad Pitt, released Wed Dec 23, so it gets 5 days in the week including Christmas. Comparable launches:
- Star-led Netflix films such as *Back in Action* and *Happy Gilmore 2* drew about 45-47M in their first week.
- Movies released after a theatrical run open lower: *Wake Up Dead Man* drew 20M in 3 days and *Frankenstein* 29M in its first week.
- *Glass Onion*, also released Dec 23, drew roughly 35M in 3 days.

The rivals are *Ray Gunn*, an animated film in its second week during the holidays, and *Emily in Paris* S6, which is likely to land in the low teens.

(e) Christmas week tops have ranged from 34M to 68M in the last three years, so the variation is large. A single breakout title like *Squid Game* S2 can double the usual result.

(f) There are no markets or expert forecasts for this week. The question creator's range is 15M to 70M.

(g) Low scenario: *Cliff Booth* underwhelms, as Fincher's films skew adult and some demand is used up by the IMAX run, and *Ray Gunn* is soft, so the top lands around 18-22M. High scenario: *Cliff Booth* becomes a holiday event, or *Ray Gunn* takes off like *KPop Demon Hunters* in its second holiday week, pushing the top to 55-70M.

For the extreme percentiles:
